column3: The Hebrew has singular “vision” and describes it as not spreading widely; BSB uses plural “visions” and calls them “scarce.”
The Hebrew says Eli’s eyes had begun to grow dim and calls his location “his place.” BSB says his eyesight “had grown so dim” and places him “in his room.”

The Hebrew uses a pronominal expression “for themselves” in the clause about the sons’ cursing; BSB explicitly names God as the object of blasphemy.

The Hebrew repeats Samuel’s name in describing his fear; BSB uses “He.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Samuel as the one called and leaves the respondent unnamed; BSB uses “him” for the one called and supplies Samuel as respondent.
The Hebrew leaves Eli unnamed and has a request particle in the prohibition. Its oath literally says “thus may God do to you, and thus may He add”; BSB makes the punishment and severity explicit.
The Hebrew leaves the replying speaker unnamed; BSB supplies Eli.
The Hebrew refers to “his words” without repeating Samuel’s name; BSB explicitly says “Samuel’s words.”

The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name three times and Shiloh twice; BSB names each once and uses pronouns for the other occurrences.
